note: Rewritten to the claim that survived the four independent audits.

problems.original_statement: FDA guidance asks sponsors to describe an approach that supports causal inference and names target trial emulation where appropriate. NICE states that some target trials cannot be adequately emulated and that bespoke data collection may then be preferable. EMA and ICH guidance emphasize fit-for-use data, prespecification and transparent non-interventional design. What none of them supplies is a threshold: how close an emulation must be to count as adequate, how much residual confounding is acceptable for a given decision, or what set of sensitivity analyses is sufficient. Sponsors therefore cannot know in advance whether a submission will be accepted, and reviewers have no consistent basis on which to accept or reject one.
problems.correction_note: The entry treated the absent thresholds as a gap to be filled. Universal numerical cutoffs for emulation adequacy, residual confounding and sensitivity-analysis sufficiency are not technically defensible, so their absence is partly correct rather than wholly a failure. The unmet need is prespecified, decision-specific criteria rather than universal ones, and benchmarking against randomized trials is supporting evidence rather than the only route to evaluation.
problems.statement: FDA guidance asks sponsors to describe an approach that supports causal inference and names target trial emulation where appropriate. NICE states that some target trials cannot be adequately emulated and that bespoke data collection may then be preferable. EMA and ICH guidance emphasize fit-for-use data, prespecification and transparent non-interventional design. None supplies an acceptance criterion, and a universal numerical cutoff for emulation adequacy, residual confounding or sensitivity-analysis sufficiency would not be technically defensible if one were offered. What is missing is the defensible version: prespecified, decision-specific criteria covering protocol fidelity, identification plausibility, data fitness, diagnostics, quantitative bias analysis and robustness of the decision itself, agreed before the submission rather than argued after it. Sponsors therefore cannot know in advance whether a submission will be accepted, and reviewers have no consistent basis to accept or reject one.
problems.why_open: The quantities that would be thresholded, residual confounding and estimand distance, are not identified from the data of the study in question, so any fixed cutoff would be applied to an unmeasurable object. A criterion has to be decision-specific because the tolerable bias depends on what the decision costs, which means the work is to build a family of criteria rather than a number. Agencies are also reasoning from a small and non-random set of precedents, so the empirical base for calibrating even a decision-specific criterion does not yet exist.
problems.proposed_direction: Build regulator-facing evidence dossiers that separate protocol fidelity, identification assumptions, data validation, diagnostics and decision robustness into distinct sections, so a reviewer can accept some and reject others rather than judging the whole. Develop prespecified, decision-specific acceptance criteria rather than universal cutoffs, agreed with the reviewer before the analysis. Conduct prospective qualification studies of data sources and phenotypes, and treat randomized-trial benchmarking as one input to calibration rather than the sole route to it, since the benchmarking corpus is a selected sample of emulable questions.

problems.original_statement: Exchangeability and consistency cannot be established from the observed data. Positivity, model behavior, balance and measurement validity can at least be diagnosed. Current reports blur the distinction: a propensity-score overlap plot is offered, and the reader is left to infer that the assumptions have been checked, when the plot bears on one of them and is silent on the rest. No standard set of diagnostics exists for an emulation, so what appears varies by author and by journal, and the absence of a diagnostic cannot be distinguished from a diagnostic that was run and not reported.
problems.correction_note: The entry drew the line in the wrong place. Positivity, model correctness and phenotype validity are not simply diagnosable: the available checks reveal or falsify particular problems and certify none of them, so the honest division is between assumptions the data cannot establish and partial diagnostics of empirical support. No single longitudinal summary is adequate for every design either, which limits what a standard panel can be.
problems.statement: Exchangeability and consistency cannot be established from observed data. Neither, strictly, can positivity, model correctness or phenotype validity: the available checks reveal or falsify particular problems and certify none of them. Current reports blur both distinctions. A propensity-score overlap plot is offered and the reader infers that the assumptions have been checked, when the plot is a partial diagnostic of one of them and silent on the rest. No standard panel exists, so what appears varies by author and by journal, and an absent diagnostic cannot be distinguished from one that was run and not reported. A single panel cannot be adequate for every design, which is a constraint on the solution rather than an argument against it.
problems.why_open: A reporting panel is a convention rather than a discovery, and conventions need an adopting body. Several components are not standardized as measurements: longitudinal balance and support by treatment history have no agreed summary statistic, and no single summary suits every design, so the panel has to be a family indexed by design rather than a fixed list. Separating what is diagnosable from what is not also makes the undiagnosable assumptions conspicuous, which is uncomfortable and is the point.
problems.proposed_direction: Define a reporting panel that separates causal assumptions the data cannot establish from partial diagnostics of empirical support, nuisance-model performance, balance, weighting, censoring, missingness and measurement validity, and state for each diagnostic what it can falsify rather than what it confirms. Standardize summary statistics for longitudinal balance and support by history, the two components with no agreed form, and index the panel by design rather than fixing one list. Pair it with the reporting checklist so a missing panel is a visible omission rather than an inference.

problems.original_statement: The assumptions an analysis needs form a ladder, and each step up adds one: from describing an association, to adjusting for measured confounders, to identifying a sustained-strategy effect, to transporting that effect to another population. A paper should identify the highest step its evidence plausibly reaches. In practice the label target trial emulation is doing that work instead: an analysis that adopts the framework is read as though it had climbed the ladder, when the framework secures the temporal alignment and nothing above it. The label has become a claim about credibility rather than a description of a design, and no convention exists for stating which step a given study actually reaches.
problems.correction_note: The ladder metaphor implies a single ordered scale, and the requirements are not ordered: consistency, conditional exchangeability, positivity, valid measurement, correct estimation and transportability are separate conditions that can hold or fail independently. A study should state them separately for its chosen estimand rather than claim a rung.
problems.statement: Target trial specification improves temporal alignment, protocol clarity and estimand definition. It does not establish consistency, conditional exchangeability, positivity, valid measurement, correct estimation or transportability, and those are separate conditions rather than steps on one scale: any of them can hold while the others fail. In practice the label does the work of all of them. An analysis that adopts the framework is read as though the whole set had been secured, and no convention asks a study to state the six requirements separately for the estimand it chose. The reporting evidence shows how weakly the label constrains the practice: of 200 published studies claiming to emulate a trial, 43% did not describe all key emulation components.
problems.why_open: The framework's value is real, which is what makes the substitution durable: naming the target trial does prevent a class of self-inflicted biases, so the label is informative and is then over-read. Stating the requirements separately needs a vocabulary that does not exist in usable form, so an author wishing to be precise has to invent the terms. Reviewers and editors also use the label as a screening heuristic, which rewards using it and penalizes qualifying it.
problems.proposed_direction: Require every emulation to state the six requirements separately for its chosen estimand, saying which are argued, which are assumed and which are diagnosed, rather than claiming a single level of credibility. Have journals ask for that statement instead of for the label, so adopting the framework is reported as a design fact and credibility is argued on its own. Audit a sample of published emulations against the six requirements to establish the current distribution, since nobody presently knows how many are argued at all.
